title: Tokenized Gold: Market Research Summary
subtitle: Nineteen tokenized gold protocols profiled end to end, and what the evidence means for the Aurumix design.
tagline: Built by founders. Designed for founders.

intro: Tokenized gold is eight years old, nineteen products deep, and far smaller than it looks. Two protocols hold roughly 86% of the sector's assets. Nine of the sixteen live products hold under $10M each, several after five or more years of trading. This is not a crowded market that Aurumix has to fight into. It is a market with two incumbents, a long tail that never found buyers, and a great deal of unoccupied ground in between.

This report profiles all nineteen protocols against the same set of questions: who issues the token, what licence covers it, where the metal sits, who verifies it, how the business is funded, what a holder actually owns, and how the product reaches customers. Every profile was built from company registers, regulator registers, issuer terms, filings and on-chain data rather than from marketing. Sixteen live protocols are covered in Section 4, three failures in Section 5, and the adjacent Indian digital gold market in Section 3.5.

findings.title: The category solved custody and never solved distribution
findings.body: Not one of the nineteen protocols runs a savings plan, a recurring purchase mechanism, or a retail referral programme. The best-provenanced product in the sector, backed by a sovereign mint with state vaults and a live proof-of-reserve feed, reached US$2.5M in four years and was shut down. Distribution is the gap, and it is where Aurumix's advantage actually sits.

findings.title: Vaulted gold cannot pay a yield, and every protocol claiming otherwise fails its own arithmetic
findings.body: Kinesis paid $26,326 in June 2026 on $310M of assets, roughly 0.10% annualised against 2.05% advertised. Pleasing Gold promises 5% on a market trading under $20 a day. MG999 advertises 2.3% net on gold borrowed at 2.5% gross with a 1.00% management fee on top. The dividend resolves into three options and there is no fourth. Section 11.1.

findings.title: The exchange premium does not survive contact with the market
findings.body: Nine protocols across the full liquidity range say a premium cannot hold: where a market is liquid, arbitrage closes it, and where it is illiquid, there is no market to express one. The two protocols trading off spot trade at a discount. The Aurumix spot capacity parameter is currently tuned to produce a 3% to 8% premium and should be re-derived. Section 11.2.

findings.title: A revenue line is a survival feature
findings.body: All three failures died of revenue starvation rather than enforcement, hacks or reserve shortfalls. Cache Gold charged a storage fee its own terms only collected on a transaction, so buy-and-hold savers paid nothing while consuming vault cost daily. Any Aurumix fee that depends on customer activity collects nothing from the customer the product is designed for.

findings.title: An anonymous bearer token cannot be wound down
findings.body: Cache Gold published a proper wind-down plan, followed it, and still stranded 96% of supply, because it had no holder registry to deliver notice to and never burned redeemed tokens. Being able to execute a wind-down requires a trustee holding title, a holder registry, burn-on-redemption, and a published reconciliation. That is the strongest argument for a permissioned token base.

findings.title: There is no cheap compliant door
findings.body: Four of nineteen protocols hold a licence covering the token they issue. The rest run one of three recognisable patterns: a software company performing regulated acts, an adjacent trade or AML registration presented as authorisation, or a regulatory halo built on a conditional approval or a distant investor. The Dubai free zone route around VARA does not exist.

findings.title: "Audited" almost never means the gold was checked
findings.body: Six protocols publish a smart-contract audit while their reserve attestation is absent, stale or self-signed. Only three have credible independent reserve examination. Separating the two explicitly in public disclosure costs nothing and is a differentiator in a sector where almost nobody does it.
